claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means do you live with him and are you the person who looks after him (for example, providing food, clothing, and care)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for him. He lives with me and I look after him - you know, making sure he's fed, clothed, all the day-to-day care that comes with raising a child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's good to know. Now I need to ask about your immigration status:

**What is your immigration status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or are you here on a visa?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, so no immigration issues there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now I need to check a few more things:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - his other parent claims Child Benefit for him. We don't live together, but Alex lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. This is a key point for your eligibility.

Let me clarify the living arrangements: **You mentioned Alex lives with you - does he live with you full-time, or does he split his time between you and his other parent?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time. His other parent doesn't live with us - we're separated - but they're the one who's claiming the Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important situation because **only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any given time**, even when parents are separated.

Since Alex lives with you full-time and you're the one responsible for his day-to-day care, you may have a stronger claim to Child Benefit than his other parent. However, the other parent is currently claiming it.

A couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Is the other parent contributing to Alex's upbringing in any way - for example, through child maintenance payments or regular contact/care arrangements?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they're not contributing financially - I'm not receiving any maintenance payments or anything like that. They don't have regular contact with Alex either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you have the right to receive Child Benefit in the UK? This is generally satisfied if you're a British citizen (which you are), but I need to confirm: have you been living in the UK, and is this where you normally live?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - this is where I normally live. I'm not living abroad or anything like that.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

**Good news - you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Here's why:

You meet all the key eligibility criteria:
- ✅ **Alex is under 16 years old** (he's 8)
- ✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - he lives with you full-time and you provide all his day-to-day care
- ✅ **You're a British citizen living in the UK** - you have the right to claim Child Benefit
- ✅ **You have the stronger claim** - Even though Alex's other parent currently claims Child Benefit for him, you have priority because Alex lives with you full-time and you're the one providing all care with no financial support or regular contact from the other parent

### What you need to know:

**Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any time.** Since the other parent is currently claiming, you'll need to make your own claim. When you do:

- HMRC will investigate and determine who has the priority claim based on who Alex lives with and who is primarily responsible for him
- In your situation, this is clearly you, so you should be awarded the Child Benefit
- The other parent's claim would then stop

### Next steps:

You should make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. You can do this online or by post using the Child Benefit claim form (CH2).
